items.title: Rumble-2-Flash: an open 0.5B speech model for 40+ languages
items.desc:
Today we're open sourcing Rumble-2-Flash under the Apache 2.0 license. It's a 0.5B-parameter speech recognition model for 40+ languages that competes with models 3-60x its size.

 
 Runs anywhere : native support in 🤗 Transformers and vLLM, no custom code 
 40+ languages : automatic language detection 
 Output control : numbers as digits or words, fillers, verbatim repeats, forced language 
 Extremely fast : an hour of audio in about half a second, with over 7,000 RTFx on full batches 
 Holds up on real phone calls : on par with NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe (30B) on a 302-hour call-centre benchmark 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Quickstart
 
 
 
 Transcribe with 🤗 Transformers 

 uv pip install torch transformers accelerate
 
 from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM

model_id = "Reson8/Rumble-2-Flash" 
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map= "auto" )

inputs = processor.apply_transcription_request(
 audio= "https://hf.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/bcn_weather.mp3" ,
 language= "English" , # omit to detect automatically 
).to(model.device, dtype=model.dtype)

output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens= 512 )
generated = output[:, inputs[ "input_ids" ].shape[- 1 ]:]
 print (processor.decode(generated, return_format= "transcription_only" )[ 0 ]) # return_format="parsed" if detecting language 
 
 audio accepts a local path, a URL, a NumPy array, or a list of these.

 

 
 
 
 
 
How it's built
 
 
 Rumble-2-Flash uses the Qwen3-ASR architecture for day-0 support. If your stack runs Transformers or vLLM, it runs Rumble-2-Flash, with no forked runtime or trust_remote_code .

items.title: Anthropic launches roadshow for proposed initial public offering
items.desc:
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
 The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 801,351,354 shares are being offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders. Anthropic also expects to grant the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of its Class A common stock.
 The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”
 The proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014. 
 A registration statement relating to these securities has been filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission but has not yet become effective. These securities may not be sold, nor may offers to buy be accepted, prior to the time the registration statement becomes effective. Today’s announcement does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

items.title: 李飞飞对话苏姿丰：AMD 收购后首次同台，CoRL 现场谈算力、机器人与「这个时代最大的失误」
items.desc:
导语：一场横跨科研、经济、AI、社会话题、算力未来的女性对话。 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 一场横跨科研、经济、AI、社会话题、算力未来的女性对话。 
 作者丨 齐铖湧 
 
 编辑丨岑 峰 
 
 2026年11月，奥斯汀，CoRL 2026的台下坐满了机器人研究者。 
 台上三把椅子，两位嘉宾，左边是即将出任AMD首席科学家的李飞飞，右边是AMD CEO苏姿丰。这是AMD收购World Labs消息传出后，两人的首次公开同台，也是李飞飞以"AMD首席科学家"身份，第一次面对整个机器人学术社区。 
 对话没有客套太久。李飞飞直接把话题引向了敏感区域：公共部门的算力"饥饿"，是" 这个历史最重要时刻最大的失误之一 "。大学和非营利机构拿不到卡，下一代研究者怎么训练？蓝天式的好奇心驱动研究怎么做？她看向苏姿丰，AMD正在建设"以吉瓦计"的算力，academia 能不能真的分到一杯羹？ 
 在苏姿丰看来：" 把一部分专门留给长期研究、留给大学，绝对是我们工作的一部分 。"但她同时也划定边界：机器人不是单靠一个端到端大模型就能啃下来的，未来需要"各种形态、各种规模"的算力，硬件、软件、系统必须协同优化。 
 不止如此，这场对话里还包含很多探讨，比如机器人会不会被基础模型一口吃掉？AGI真的只差"一分钟"了吗？在这个连PhD都要被AI重新定义的时代，做学术还有没有意义？ 
 以下是AI科技评论带来的完整对话实录。 
 李飞飞、苏姿丰（Lisa Su）和主持人Peter Stone（从左往右） 
 01 
 
 
 
 物理 AI 带来的机会：数千亿美元量级 
 
 Peter Stone： 谢谢二位，Lisa、Fei-Fei，来到CoRL。精彩的演讲，那个视频（Atlas最新成果）我们明天都等着看，大家现在都坐不住了。接下来大约半小时，我们会从Slido（现场提问平台）上取问题，我也会混入一些事先准备的问题。 
 Lisa、Fei-Fei，你们现在和机器人学习社区同台。我们已经听说了AMD收购World Labs的事（正在进行中），Fei-Fei刚才也讲了世界模型和前方的巨大机会。Lisa，我先问你：AMD一直从数据中心到边缘和嵌入式系统，在整个AI栈上投资。 
 Peter Stone： 展望机器人和物理AI，你认为AMD最大的机会在哪里？World Labs如何融入这个更大的战略？ 
 苏姿丰： 谢谢Peter，也谢谢大家让我来。Fei-Fei邀请我来"蹭会"，希望没关系。欢迎大家来到奥斯汀。 
 我认为这是AI极其激动人心的时刻。回顾我们迄今取得的所有进展，我们其实还处在可能性的非常早期的阶段（very early innings）。物理AI、尤其是机器人，是巨大的机会，对我们来说，未来几年这是 数千亿美元量级的机遇 。关键在于，你必须真正理解物理、模型和整个环境。所以我们非常高兴Fei-Fei和World Labs团队加入AMD。 
 苏姿丰： 除了她是超级明星之外，我们能不能就直说她是超级明星？（全场笑）在我们这个行业，硬件优化要持续很多年，你对工作负载了解得越多、越清楚它要往哪走，就越好。我一直说的 硬件、软件、系统协同优化 的愿景，放在机器人上尤为适用。未来5到10年，这将是极其重要的领域。更重要的是，对整个AMD生态而言，我们非常希望把AMD的开放生态扩展到在座的整个机器人社区。谢谢大家给我几分钟。 
 Peter Stone： 太好了。我们能看出她是超级明星，因为她是Yuke和Roberto的博士和博后导师，正是他们帮忙促成了这届大会，除此之外她还有很多成功的学生。 
 Fei-Fei，换你。从你的角度，加入AMD如何扩展World Labs能做的事？你刚阐述了世界模型的愿景，这个结合让你们接下来能构建什么？对机器人社区意味着什么？ 
 李飞飞： 首先，来到奥斯汀太好了。我在台下跟朋友说，我知道我以后会常来奥斯汀。 
 我认识Lisa很多年了，说到超级明星，我们大约十年前认识。想想Lisa过去十年为AMD、为计算世界所做的一切，再到现在这个AI时代，真的令人叹为观止。建模与计算的关系，在AI中已经根本性地改变了。 
 现在我满世界跑，普通人，不是在座各位，问我：AI到底是什么？我的回答是： AI就是计算，计算就是AI 。 无论是世界模型还是语言模型，坦白说，我们正在看到大量单模态和多模态模型的融合。正如Lisa所说，这要求硬件与软件之间的协同设计与协同演化。这是一个极其有意思的机会。 
 我还想对台下的博士生、硕士生、本科生说：做科学的方式也在演变。 AI不仅是一个待解决的问题，也是工具。我们正身处"团队科学"（team science）的激动人心的时代。把World Labs的实力和AMD的实力结合起来，以
items.summary: 李飞飞与苏姿丰在 CoRL 2026 对话。李飞飞指出公共部门算力饥饿是重大失误，苏姿丰称 AMD 将建设吉瓦级算力，部分资源留给学术长期研究，并强调物理 AI 需软硬系统协同。
items.reason: 这是 AMD 收购 World Labs 后关键人物首次公开对话，不仅确认了战略方向，更直接给出了学术界获取顶级算力的官方承诺，填补了厂商意图与市场现实的认知空白。

items.title: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run
items.desc:
Hugging Face and OpenRouter are teaming up to make open-weight models easy to run. Every major open-weight release is already being published on the Hugging Face Hub, and OpenRouter serves those models at scale, routing each request across 80+ providers based on live measurements of each one. Together, every open-weight model on the Hub that a provider serves can be called with your Hugging Face token, through the same API, with the best provider picked for each request.

 Today, we are switching Inference Providers from our own custom router to OpenRouter's. Requests made to language models now go through OpenRouter, which picks the best provider for each call based on live price, speed and reliability, and retries on another provider if the first one fails. Your code stays the same.

 
 
 
 
 
Run them with the tools you already use
 
 
 The router supports OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs and Anthropic's Messages API for every chat model, whatever the provider behind it. Pick your coding agent or SDK and a model, then copy the steps, or copy the whole setup as a prompt for your agent:

 

 Setup guides for Claude Code , Codex , OpenCode , Pi and Hermes Agent 

 The same Hugging Face token also gives you storage with Storage Buckets , compute with Jobs and dedicated inference with Inference Endpoints . PRO, Team and Enterprise plans include monthly credits for compute and inference.

 
 
 
 
 
How open-weight models are used
 
 
 On OpenRouter, open-weight models went from 26.8% of the tokens served in October 2025 to 71.7% at the end of September 2026, after peaking at 77.5% in July ( OpenRouter, October 2026 ). Over the same period, weekly open-weight volume grew more than 60-fold, against almost tenfold for closed models. This week, the most used model on OpenRouter is an open-weight one, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, with 59.2 trillion tokens ( rankings ).

 
 
 
 

 Open-weight models cost about four times less on average: $0.28 per million input toke

items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
items.desc:
Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Neon — bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.
 Neon ranks ahead of comparable models and #3 overall with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level, landing just behind larger, slower models. On the Vals Index , Neon ranks #2 and lands on the Pareto frontier. Beyond just pushing on raw model capability, we’re continuing to make our models better to work with, Neon ranks #2 on steerability (adapting cleanly to mid-task user corrections) on the new Agent Arena Index . Neon also excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing.
 The model is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.
 Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out today in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio , Gemini for business (via API and model dropdown), for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , and for Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app .
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 
 

 
 
 Delivers across enterprise, analytical, and scientific work Enterprise work lives in spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video. Neon can synthesize across all of these inputs in a single 1 million-token context window and turns inputs into structured deliverables. Independent evaluations rank Neon as one of the top models and on benchmarks like the Vals Index , it ranks #2 (70.9%), and reaches #1 on both the Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench .
 Neon also shows strong wins across categories on Surge AI , ranking #1 on most benchmarks across finance, accounting, spreadsheet modeling, and complex constraint following. It also scores 73.5% on Chartography for reading

items.title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
items.desc:
Today we are releasing DaisyRose-27B , RadixArk’s first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using Miles . We trained it on long-horizon agent tasks with sessions up to 1M tokens, with just 1,200 curated tasks in 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs. DaisyRose-27B improves Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 from 5.6% to 12.0% . Beyond Terminal-Bench 4.1, it also delivers gains on a variety of other reasoning, instruction following, and coding benchmarks.

 The checkpoints are available under Apache 2.0 :

 
 BF16 
 FP8 
 NVFP4 
 
 The model retains Qwen3.8-27B’s architecture, tokenizer, chat template, image understanding, and 256K-token context window . The longer training sessions use harness summarization to span multiple trajectories. See the model card for model properties and inference settings.

 
 
 
 
 
Run DaisyRose-27B
 
 
 We recommend serving DaisyRose-27B with SGLang and DSpark speculative decoding. The SGLang cookbook provides launch configurations for different GPUs and checkpoint formats.

 After starting the server with the served model name DaisyRose-27B on port 30000 , you can send a request using the OpenAI Python client:

 from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
 base_url= "http://localhost:30000/v1" ,
 api_key= "none" ,
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
 model= "DaisyRose-27B" ,
 messages=[
 {
 "role" : "user" ,
 "content" : "How many positive divisors does 360 have?" ,
 }
 ],
 temperature= 1.0 ,
 top_p= 0.95 ,
 extra_body={ "top_k" : 20 , "min_p" : 0.0 },
)

 print (response.choices[ 0 ].message.reasoning_content)
 print (response.choices[ 0 ].message.content)
 
 The model thinks before answering by default. Its reasoning is returned in reasoning_content , and its final answer in content . These settings follow the model card’s quickstart .

items.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
items.desc: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and activation memory. CPU affinity and core isolation further reduce host scheduling interference. Together, these mechanisms support the pretraining of a 285B-parameter model on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards, providing a concrete setting for the architectural and systems studies. For post-training, we introduce TeleGym, a unified agent execution platform that connects execution, evaluation, and trajectory construction to policy optimization. Disaggregated asynchronous execution, bounded oversampling, and partial rollout accommodate heterogeneous task durations while preserving trajectory continuity across policy updates. Together, these advances establish an Ascend-oriented training foundation for the continued development of Xing 4 across model scales and increasingly demanding reasoning and agent workloads.
items.titleCn: TeleChat to Xing4：国产芯片上的前沿 Agentic 模型

items.descZh: 我们推出了 Xing 4，这是一系列大型语言模型，通过在昇腾（Ascend）上的模型架构和训练基础设施的协同进展，扩展了 TeleChat 血脉。本报告描述了该系列背后的设计原则和系统工程，涵盖架构选择、大规模预训练以及推理和智能体后训练。我们研究了稀疏激活、注意力设计、模型深度与宽度以及投机解码如何在模型容量与计算、内存访问和执行开销之间取得平衡。我们的预训练基础设施建立在 MindSpore HyperParallel 之上，结合了拓扑感知的混合分片、高效的分布式优化器执行，以及对长序列工作负载和激活内存的协同管理。CPU 亲和性和核心隔离进一步减少了主机调度干扰。这些机制共同支持了在 8,192 张昇腾 910C 卡上对一个 2850 亿参数模型进行预训练，为架构和系统研究提供了具体的环境。在后训练方面，我们引入了 TeleGym，这是一个统一的智能体执行平台，将执行、评估和轨迹构建与策略优化连接起来。解构

items.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
items.desc: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer? Given minimal guidance, ten labeled examples, and a sandbox, mainly on multiple-choice questions, we task three frontier LLMs with either generating the weights of a fixed architecture or designing the architecture themselves. When free to design, all three compile plain-text facts into a sparse table queried by a fixed procedure, reaching up to 54.4% test accuracy. An LLM-designed model achieves higher test accuracy than the most accurate released Transformer that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800x fewer parameters. Without gradients, they choose a table, in which the LLM can state what each weight means and can find and rewrite a wrong one. Each wrong answer points to one row, and removing a row changes about one other answer. From this, we propose an associative-memory-based model up to 17x faster on GPUs than a same-sized Transformer. We also test pretrained weights, other benchmarks, and tasks where models generate answers. Pretrained LLMs remain more accurate; the claim concerns which structure to build when writing weights.
items.titleCn: 权重空间编程：LLM 设计非 Transformer 架构
items.summary: 研究 LLM 在无梯度下降情况下手写权重或设计架构。LLM 倾向于使用稀疏表而非 Transformer，参数减少 1800 倍且准确率更高。基于关联内存的新模型在 GPU 上比同规模 Transformer 快 17 倍。
items.reason: 挑战“Transformer 是唯一最优解”的认知，展示 LLM 自主架构设计能力，提供无梯度训练下的架构选型新思路，具有理论突破意义。
items.descZh: 诸如 Transformer 等标准神经架构之所以被选中，是因为它们能够很好地通过梯度下降进行训练并在 GPU 上快速运行。在权重空间编程中，大型语言模型（LLM）无需基于梯度的训练即可手写目标权重，因此这些原因不再适用。我们还应该保留 Transformer 吗？在极少指导、十个带标签示例和一个沙盒的条件下，主要针对多项式选择题，我们让三个前沿 LLM 生成固定架构的权重或自行设计架构。当可以自由设计时，所有三个模型都将纯文本事实编译成通过固定程序查询的稀疏表，测试准确率最高可达 54.4%。LLM 设计的模型在使用的参数少约 1,800 倍的同时，实现了比同一 LLM 编写的最准确的已发布 Transformer 更高的测试准确率。在没有梯度的情况下，它们选择了一个表，其中 LLM 可以阐明每个权重的含义，并能找到并重写错误的权重。每个错误的答案都指向一行，删除一行大约会改变另一个答案。基于此，我们提出了一种基于联想记忆的模型，在 GPU 上比同尺寸的 Transformer 快达 17 倍。我们还测试了预训练

items.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
items.desc: Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch given a language specification. Its Environment Evolution Loop optimizes a multiplicative objective combining validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope through proxy feedback. RepoFactory produces 10,159 environments across 17 software domains. Training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on these environments yields RepoHorizen-35B-A3B, which achieves gains of 22.6 percentage points on NL2Repo-Bench and 8.5 points on average across five benchmarks covering long-horizon coding and agentic tasks in real-world production settings, compared with 17.5 and 6.4 points without environment evolution. These results highlight the training value of RepoFactory environments and the additional gains from the Environment Evolution Loop.
items.titleCn: RepoFactory：自动化构建长时程编码 Agent 环境
items.summary: 提出 RepoFactory 管道，将真实代码仓库转化为可验证训练环境，生成 10,159 个跨 17 个领域的环境。在 Qwen3.5-35B 上训练后，模型在 NL2Repo-Bench 上提升 22.6 个百分点。
items.reason: 解决长时程编码任务缺乏高质量可验证环境的核心痛点，提供具体的环境数量和性能增益数据，可直接用于 Agent 训练数据合成。
items.descZh: 为长程任务训练编程智能体需要具备可验证反馈的环境。现有的流水线通常采用以验证结束的线性流程，虽能确立可用性，但对提升训练价值的指导意义微乎其微。递归自我改进（RSI）通常需要模型展开（rollouts）或模型训练以及后续的下游评估，在长程任务中，成本和反馈延迟会被放大。我们如何才能使用及时、可靠的代理信号来提升训练价值并在规模化环境中合成环境？我们提出了 RepoFactory，这是一个自动化的流水线，它将真实的代码库转换为可验证的环境，让智能体根据语言规范从头构建完整的项目。其环境演化回路（Environment Evolution Loop）通过代理反馈，优化了结合有效性、结构耦合和实现范围的乘性目标。RepoFactory 在 17 个软件领域中生成了 10,159 个环境。在这些环境上训练 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B，得到了 RepoHorizen-35B-A3B，它在 NL2Repo-Bench 上取得了 22.6 个百分点的提升，并在涵盖真实世界长程编程和智能体任务的五个基准测试中平均取得了 8.5 点的提升

 Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.

 Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. items.title: 派早报：国区 App Store 将 AIGC 合规设为上架必填、OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 等
items.desc:
国区 App Store 将 AIGC 合规材料设为上架必填 11 月 16 日，有开发者反馈苹果在 App Store Connect 后台新增「人工智能生成或合成内容（AIGC）服务声明与备案信息」与「已完成安全评估的证明」2 项中国大陆分发必填项。此举将 2026 年审核指南的生成式 AI 条款变为提交入口的强制执行，合规材料从建议变成上架的前置条件。含 AIGC 服务的 App 需提交备案及安全评估报告副本。若使用第三方技术或模型，还须提供授权或盖章合作协议与算法备案号。新 App 需立即提交，现有 App 须在 2027 年 1 月 31 日前完成。 来源 
 OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 与 Sol 模型 OpenAI 于当地时间 11 月 17 日发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 与 GPT-6.2 Sol，两款模型同日上线 ChatGPT Work、Codex 与 API。官方称两款模型都能用更少的输出 token 完成高难度任务，用户在同一付费额度内可以完成更多工作。
 Astra 定位为处理最难项目的模型，官方推荐用于文档、演示文稿、编码等专业场景。它可以用一张幻灯片截图当模板，匹配其版式、配色甚至字号，生成风格一致的整套演示文稿。在 Codex 一侧，Astra 更擅长在既有项目中做修改与测试，官方称早期测试者反馈代码风格更干净、测试更聚焦、返工轮次更少。Sol 则定位为日常编码与写作中更便宜的模型。Cognition 的 FrontierCode 2.0 测试衡量「对真实代码库的改动是否达到维护者可合并的标准」，两款模型都开到最高推理力度时，Sol 的成绩只比 Astra 低半分，成本约为 Astra 的五分之一。
 两款模型即日起向 Plus、Pro、Enterprise、Edu 用户开放，覆盖 ChatGPT Work 与 Codex。Ultrafast 高速模式首次向每月 200 美元的 Pro 档开放，先支持 Sol；每月 500 美元的 Pro 档与 Enterprise、Edu 工作区可对两款模型使用，后者需由管理员开启。官方称该模式生成速度最高为标准速率的 4.5 倍，但更消耗使用额度，可在模型选择器中切换。API 定价按每百万 token 计，Astra 输入 8 美元、缓存输入 0.4 美元、输出 40 美元，比上一代 GPT-6 Astra 的标准输入输出价格低 20%；Sol 维持 GPT-6.1 定价，输入 2 美元、缓存输入 0.1 美元、输出 10 美元。 来源 
 iPhone Duo 测试 2D 人脸解锁功能 iOS 27.3 开发者测试版新增「用前置摄像头解锁」选项，iPhone Duo 可用 2D 人脸识别解锁屏幕。设置过程与 Face ID 类似，但无需缓慢转头，只需把头向左、右、上、下各转 1 次，约 5 秒完成；解锁速度约 0.5 秒，环境非常暗的情况下会解锁失败。同时，因为 iPhone Duo 不具备 TrueDepth 相机的红外深度图，苹果在设置时也会提示该功能「不如 Touch ID 或 Face ID 安全」，理论上可被照片或视频欺骗，实测每次欺骗解锁失败后下次解锁会强制要求 Touch ID，画面无人脸则不强制。该功能只能用于锁屏解锁，使用 Apple Pay、安装或登录应用仍需 Touch ID 或密码。 来源 
 此外，iOS 27.3 开发者测试版也为国行 iPad 和 Mac 新增「Apple 智能」，支持搭载 M 系列芯片的 Mac 和 iPad 以及采用 A17 Pro 与 A20 Pro 芯片的 iPad mini，但国行版本不包含 Siri AI。 来源 
 松下发布紧凑型电影摄影机 SHX1 11 月 17 日，松下发布紧凑型电影摄影机 LUMIX SHX1，型号为 AU-SHX1。该机采用带光学低通滤镜的 6K 全画幅部分堆栈式 CMOS 传感器，可减轻果冻效应并支持高帧率录制配合双原生 ISO 与动态范围增强，该机在 V-Log 下动态范围达 15 档；预装 ARRI LogC3，用户可在 V-Log 与 ARRI LogC3 之间按调色流程选择；该机无需外接录机即可录制 2 种 RAW 格式，可将 Apple ProRes RAW 内录至 CFexpress Type B 卡，也是首个支持直接向外部 SSD 录制 Blackmagic RAW 的 LUMIX 机型，素材无需转码即可在 DaVinci Resolve 中直接剪辑，并可选用 Blackmagic 色彩科学。此外，该机还在 LUMIX 中首次支持 Open Gate 录制 Blackmagic RAW 6K 24p。
 机身方面，LUMIX SH
items.summary: 国区 App Store 强制要求 AIGC 备案与安全评估。OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 与 Sol，Astra 擅长复杂任务与演示生成，Sol 低成本适合日常。API 降价 20%，Pro 档开放 Ultrafast 模式，速度提升 4.5 倍。
items.reason: 聚合了监管政策（AIGC 强制备案）与模型发布（GPT-6.2 系列）两大关键信息，特别是具体的 API 定价与性能对比数据，对需要决策模型选型及合规开发的开发者极具时效性参考价值。

items.title: 李飞飞最新 CoRL2026 演讲实录：从「橱柜模型」到世界模型，机器人需要什么样的 AI ？
items.desc:
导语：时隔两年，World Labs 的工作已经完全不同了。 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 时隔两年，World Labs 的工作已经完全不同了。 
 作者丨 齐铖湧 
 
 编辑丨岑 峰 
 
 2026年11月，CoRL（机器人学习顶会）在奥斯汀开幕。 这一届的演讲嘉宾，有一个无法回避的名字，李飞飞。斯坦福教授、ImageNet发起者、World Labs创始人。就在本届CoRL之前，World Labs被AMD收购的消息正在圈内发酵，她即将出任AMD首席科学家。这届CoRL现场，她不仅全面介绍了World Labs最近的工作和她的行业观点，还邀请AMD苏妈参与了对话圆桌，某种意义上，这是她的"AMD首秀"。 
 为她做开场介绍的，是她的学生、本届CoRL组织者之一Yuke（朱玉可）。他讲了一个细节：毕业典礼上，李飞飞对他说，“你在我的实验室时是我的学生，但从今往后，你是我的朋友。” 
 这场演讲的正式主角，是World Labs与斯坦福团队研发的新模型Atlas：一个统一的生成与重建世界模型。 
 以下是AI科技评论带来的现场实录。 
 ▎ 《Atlas：A Unified World Model for Generation and Reconstruction》 
 ▎ 分享者：李飞飞 
 非常荣幸受邀来到CoRL，尤其是有好几位我的前学生都是组织者。你们干得真棒，我知道，因为我很多论文和工作坊提案都被你们拒了。（全场笑）向CoRL致敬。 
 今天我想分享我们实验室最近开发的一个模型，叫Atlas：一个统一的生成与重建世界模型。 
 既然在CoRL，就先从机器人学的动机讲起。 
 机器人领域最近变化很大，但不管我们用什么方法，机器人要解决的根本问题是：给定世界状态、给定目标、给定机器人，每一个时刻下一步该做什么？ 
 大体上，机器人需要解决几个问题：第一，理解和表示世界的状态，用隐式还是显式可以讨论，但"理解"本身很重要；第二，预测有后果的动作，并加以规划。雷峰网 
 最后，数据永远是难题。机器人是典型的长尾问题，成功部署极其受限，所以我们总希望能通过尽可能多地模拟不同环境来补充真实数据，用于训练和评估。 
 无论用什么方法，这三个问题在机器人学里都依然重要。而它们恰好对应世界模型要解决的问题：理解环境，对应渲染；预测动作后果，对应规划；模拟世界状态，对应仿真。 
 渲染、规 划与仿真， 世界模型的三大维度 
 我不想教条地说它们完全独立，实际上它们在很多方面可以统一、彼此衔接，这些都是这个领域最前沿、最令人兴奋的方向。 
 今天我要专门讲的Atlas，主要解决渲染和仿真问题，尤其是模拟世界的几何以及3D/4D动态。 
 简而言之，Atlas是一个从零训练的自回归基础模型，单一模型，接收多模态输入，文本、图像、视频、深度信号、灰度框（graybox）或3D结构信号。它输出像素帧；不仅生成时空上漂亮的帧，还能合成新视角，从而实现高精度、高保真的3D重建。 
 Atlas：聚焦于渲染和仿真 
 先回顾一点历史。 
 计算机视觉有两个非常重要的问题，研究者们花了几代人的时间去理解。 
 一是3D重建问题，从经典的"Building Rome in a Day"到最近的NeRF类神经渲染工作，根本问题是：给定不同相机位姿下的图像，构建符合真实世界的3D世界。大多数方法需要大量带位姿的图像；位姿覆盖不足时，重建出的区域就充满不确定性。 
 经典三维重建的问题所在 
 另一条线是生成式AI。扩散架构天然适合多视角生成的探索，让我们离"生成+重建"越来越近。已有不少出色工作尝试联合去噪多个视角来保持空间一致性，但总体结果有限：空间一致性难维持，且每次去噪只对应固定目标视角，计算昂贵、无法实时。 
 经典三维重建很难维持空间一致性 
 改变视角或实时运行，计算成本太高 
 Atlas延续这条思路，试图用一个模型架构、一套训练配方，把生成与重建统一在同一个屋檐下。 
 它是这样做的，首先是一个极端：给定多张图像，Atlas做重建；图像足够多时，做稠密重建，很好地恢复场景。另一个极端：零像素条件，只给一个文本提示，Atlas做纯生成，并生成多帧视角一致的图像。 
 Atlas还能做连接两端的事：我们称之为稀疏重建：只给极少量视角，极端情况只有一张图，Atlas能估计相机位姿，再生成尽可能多的视角，重建并生成完整世界。它在一个模型内，从稠密重建到稀疏重建再到纯生成，自由切换。 
 看个例子。 
 在座至少有人认得，这是斯坦福校园著名的主广场（Main Quad）。给定两张有限的图像，模型"幻觉"出一个主广场，熟悉斯坦福的人知道，这不是真的主广场，它"神似"但不是：有一点那些拱廊的影子，大部分是生成的。 
 给8张图，效果好得多，相对
items.summary: 李飞飞在 CoRL2026 发布 World Labs 新模型 Atlas，一个统一的生成与重建世界模型。它接收多模态输入，解决机器人领域的理解、预测及仿真问题，支持渲染、规划与模拟环境。
items.reason: 揭示了世界模型在机器人领域的最新技术进展，Atlas 模型将生成与重建统一，为具身智能的数据获取与环境模拟提供了新的范式，是理解机器人 AI 前沿方向的重要资料。

items.title: 刚刚，谷歌Gemini 4再发新款，对标超越GPT-6.2 Sol，世界模型Genie 4也已开放
items.desc:
一觉醒来，谷歌又双叒叕发 Gemini 4 模型了。

 谷歌最近一直在基础模型上发力，从最高智能到最高效率的模型不停发布，为了重返王座真是拼了。

 在 Carbon、Argon、Hydrogen 之后，填补最高智能和最高效率之间的 「中杯」模型 Gemini 4 Neon 登场！ 

 

 Demis Hassabis 称，Gemini 4 Neon 这一中杯模型，是 「Alchemy at its finest（炼金术的杰作）」 。

 Gemini 4 家族中，Carbon 是旗舰，负责最难的长程项目；Hydrogen 面向日常高频场景，追求的是响应速度。 Neon 的定位在二者中间，「在复杂编程、分析推理和生产级企业工作流上提供前沿推理能力，同时更快、更省」 。

 Neon 速度是 Carbon 的 3 倍，成本只有 Carbon 的 60%。 定价每百万输入 token 3 美元，每百万输出 token 15 美元，缓存输入 token 低至 0.15 美元，上下文窗口 100 万 token，另外支持 4 档可调的思考深度，开发者可以按任务复杂度灵活切换速度和推理深度。

 博客链接：https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/

 全面跑分 
 Neon 在第三方评测上的表现相当全面。综合智能方面， 它在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上以 61 分排到第 3 ，仅落后于更大、更慢的模型；在 Vals Index 上排第 2（70.9%），落在帕累托前沿上。

 

 在全新的 Agent Arena Index 中，Neon 凭借 4200 余个真实世界智能体会话拿下第 2（1336 分），可操控性（steerability）同样排第 2，意味着用户中途改口时，模型能更干净地调整方向。

 企业和知识工作类的评测更是大面积刷榜。Legal Research Bench 和 Tax Agent Bench 两项第 1，Surge AI 覆盖的金融、会计、电子表格建模等多个类目也大多排在第 1。Zapier AutomationBench 第 1（56.3%），Andon Labs 的 Vending-Bench 2 同样第 1（$16,843），后者是一个模拟长周期商业经营的测试，对长程规划能力要求很高。密集图表阅读基准 Chartography 得分 73.5%，Agents' Last Exam v1.1 得分 75.8%，与头部模型持平。

 科学和数学推理方向上，Neon 拿下了 Terminal-Bench Science（70.5%）、RiemannBench（84.0%）和 HLE-Diamond（71.3%）三项第一，均为同类最佳。

 

 逐项拆解 Neon 能力 
 根据官方博客，Neon 的新能力可以归纳为几个大方向。

 写代码，更准更稳。 Neon 面向真实生产环境，能处理多文件调试、重构和精准编辑。谷歌特别提到了它的「surgical edits（手术式编辑）」能力，能对多文件项目做定点修改。模型在多步骤指令遵循上有明显提升，同时在内部 Google Antigravity 测试中录得了 迄今为止最低的编造率 （fabrication rate）。

 100 万 token 窗口拿下多模态。 电子表格、PDF、图表、音频、视频，Neon 可以在一个上下文窗口里同时消化这些输入，输出结构化的交付物。「Neon 在整体质量上追平甚至超过了 Carbon，速度快 3 倍，成本降低 40%。它在准确性、细节和速度之间找到了令人信服的平衡。」

 网络安全方向。 这是 Neon 本次发布中一个独特的动作。谷歌推出了 Neon for Cyber，覆盖安全代码编写、漏洞发现、漏洞验证和漏洞修补的完整链条。

 从数据看，AutoBaxBench 安全代码生成在困难级别达到 SOTA（76%），全面超越 Carbon；WebExploitBench v1.2 渗透测试同样 SOTA（51.26%），成本仅为竞品大模型的一半；S EC -bench Pro 漏洞发现 SOTA（90.5%），单挑战成本约为同类的一半；CWE-bench v2 漏洞修补 70.7%，比 Carbon 提升 3.4%。Neon for Cyber 将在未来几天内通过 Fairwind Program 向受信任的安全防御人员开放。

 

 

 安全对齐，几乎「零作弊」。 谷歌在安全性上下了重注。Terminal-B
items.summary: 谷歌发布中端模型 Gemini 4 Neon，速度为旗舰 Carbon 的 3 倍，成本仅为其 60%。定价每百万输入 3 美元，上下文 100 万 token，支持 4 档思考深度，多项企业级评测排名前列。
items.reason: 详细拆解了 Gemini 4 家族中新模型的定位、定价策略及在 Agent 场景下的具体跑分优势，为寻找高性价比替代 Opus 或 Sol 的开发者提供了精确的技术选型参考。

items.title: 刚刚，Gemini 4 Neon 突袭发布，性价比一夜斩杀 Opus 5.5
items.desc:
不得不佩服 Gemini 挑日子发新闻的勇气，昨晚《GTA 6》刚解锁上线把全球互联网热搜屠了个干净，劈柴老哥今天依然顶着漫天游戏贴，硬生生从元素周期表里又掏出了一款新模型。

 

 就在刚刚，距离上一款旗舰模型 Gemini 4 Carbon 发布才过去三周， 谷歌反手端出了全新的主力大模型 Gemini 4 Neon，也就是化学元素周期表里的第 10 号稀有气体「氖」。 

 

 最让开发者松了一口气的是，谷歌这次没有再搞排队申请那套期货玩法，发布当天就同步在 Google AI Studio、Gemini App、企业端 API 以及自家的编程环境 Google Antigravity 里 全量现货上线。 

 先给大伙划个省流重点。

 如果说三周前的 Carbon 是用来冲击超长程复杂任务的扛把子模型，那么今天登场的 Neon， 就是谷歌真正派出来跟 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 贴身肉搏的走量性价比主力。 

 它不仅在 Artificial Analysis 综合智商榜上 拿下了 61 分的高分 ，定价还直接压到了每百万输入 Token 3 美元（缓存输入低至 0.15 美元）、输出 15 美元，同时标配 100 万上下文窗口。

 

 连 R 星都知道按时交货了，谷歌自然也不好意思再发期货了。

 Gemini 4 家族排座次，Neon 凭什么坐上 C 位 
 聊模型能力之前，不得不先吐槽一下谷歌现在这门让人眼花缭乱的化学命名学。以前大模型起名，大家顶多在 Pro、Max、Ultra 和 Flash 之间排列组合，虽然俗套，但用户一眼就能看明白谁强谁弱。

 现在，ChatGPT 是天文系，Claude 是文学 / 诗歌文体系，而到了 Gemini 4 世代，谷歌干脆一头扎进了元素周期表，先后掏出了1号「氢」Hydrogen、18号「氩」Argon、6号「碳」Carbon，以及今天的10号「氖」Neon。

 属实是集齐数理化文科综合卷了。 

 连 Google DeepMind 自家的研究员姚顺宇今天都在 X 上调侃，说用化学元素当代号简直是个天才主意，每次代号泄露的时候，看着网友们一头雾水、完全搞不清这模型到底是哪个档位、该跟谁对标，实在太有意思了。

 

 为了防止大伙彻底看晕，谷歌这次终于在官方图谱里把 Gemini 4 家族的排座次给交代清楚了。

 从官方公布的家族定位表来看，主力梯队被切成了清晰的左中右三档。 

 最右侧的 Hydrogen 主攻日常高频编程与轻量 Agent 工作流，AA 智商指数 54 分，每百万输入和输出只要 1.5 美元和 7.5 美元，面向所有人开放。

 最左侧的 Carbon 专啃最硬的超长程大项目与深度研究，AA 智商指数 60 分，标准定价是每百万输入 4 美元、输出 20 美元（11 月 30 日前促销价为 2 美元和 10 美元），主要面向高阶的 Ultra 订阅用户。

 

 而今天发布的 Neon 正好卡在正中间的黄金甜点位，主攻软件工程、知识工作与科学推理，Pro 和 Ultra 两档用户都能直接用。

items.title: Limite 1B - Violetto: Technical Report
items.desc:
arXiv:2611.21646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Limite 1B - Violetto, a one-billion-parameter model designed for high-throughput mathematical reasoning. Limite is trained from scratch on 237 billion tokens from a carefully curated, mathematics-centric corpus and supports context lengths of up to 131k tokens. Its architecture and training recipe were developed together to maximize reasoning capability while keeping training and inference costs low. Post-training combines knowledge distillation, targeted supervised fine-tuning, and RLVR on a curated curriculum. Limite achieves 94.01% on AIME 2026 and 74.25% on BeyondAIME, placing it among models many times its size on our evaluation suite. The model is deliberately only lightly instruction-tuned: it is intended primarily as a single-turn mathematical solver and as a fast, parallel component of larger systems, rather than as a general-purpose assistant. We release the model, its base and value checkpoints, and an optimized serving implementation under the Apache 2.0 license.

items.summary: 发布 1B 参数数学推理模型 Limite 1B，基于 2370 亿 token 训练，支持 131k 上下文。在 AIME 2026 得分 94.01%，BeyondAIME 得分 74.25%，性能远超同规模模型，并以 Apache 2.0 开源。

items.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
items.desc: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.

items.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
items.desc: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. We further present the data and training recipe underlying these capabilities, together with empirical studies of key design choices. Code and models are available at https://github.com/yyfz/Pi4.

items.title: MInfoVisQA: A Multilingual Benchmark for Information-Rich Visual Question Answering
items.desc:
arXiv:2611.21644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel in vision-language tasks; yet, whether they maintain consistent understanding of information-rich visuals (InfoVis) when the surface language changes remains unclear. To quantify this capability, we introduce MInfoVisQA, a parallel benchmark with 8,960 QA configurations derived from 128 seed instances across 24 languages. We construct seed-matched, language-parallel visuals and QA pairs by disentangling numerical-structural data from text and programmatically synchronizing translated labels. We evaluate 25 MLLMs under two settings: Language-Aligned QA (LQA, matching visual-text languages) and Cross-Language QA (XQA, fixed QA language with varying visual languages). The results show that aggregate accuracy masks substantial robustness gaps: two models with comparable mean LQA accuracy (80.4\%) exhibit performance spreads of 7.8 and 20.3 percentage points across languages. Moreover, all 25 models score lower with non-English visuals under fixed English QA, underscoring the need for cross-language sensitivity metrics.

items.title: Show HN: 100ms copy-on-write workspaces for AI agents on macOS
items.desc:
[![Image 1: Replica Banner](https://github.com/gabrielvfonseca/replica/raw/main/banner.jpg)](https://github.com/gabrielvfonseca/replica/blob/main/banner.jpg)

## Isolated replicas of your workspace for AI agents

[](https://github.com/gabrielvfonseca/replica#isolated-replicas-of-your-workspace-for-ai-agents)
**Replica gives every agent run its own fully installed copy of your project, created in milliseconds with APFS copy-on-write. Each copy is a real git checkout, and automatic cleanup keeps total disk use bounded.**

cd "$(replica new --ttl 2h --name fix-login)" # a ready workspace; the path goes to stdout
git checkout -b agent/fix-login && git commit -am "fix login" && git push -u origin agent/fix-login
replica rm # done; or let the TTL expire 

## Why

[](https://github.com/gabrielvfonseca/replica#why)
Agent workloads are dominated by creating and deleting small files (a checkout, `node_modules`, build output), and that's where macOS is slowest. A fresh install takes seconds to minutes before the agent does any work.

Replica builds a **base** once: a git clone with its dependencies installed. Each `replica new` clones that base with one `clonefile(2)` call. The data blocks stay shared with the base until a file changes, so the new workspace is ready almost at once. Measured on an Apple M1 Max, `replica new` of a 1,700-file project takes about 100 ms at N = 1 and about 230 ms at N = 10 concurrent workspaces, versus seconds for `git clone` plus an install. items.title: Inside the Codex sandbox
items.desc: sandboxing an MCP server Codex sandbox implementation Network proxy macOS Linux Windows Building on the Codex sandbox At OpenAI, we take a defense in depth approach when it comes to safeguarding agents. While our investments in training and alignment are fundamental to this effort, we also implement features in our agentic harness, Codex , to provide additional protections. Because one of the most common (and potentially risky) things Codex does is run commands on your computer, we built the Codex sandbox so Codex can work in your existing environment within filesystem and network limits you control. A sandbox limits what a program can access while it runs. For a photo-organizing task, you might configure the Codex sandbox to let commands read and modify files in ~/Pictures while blocking network access to prevent uploads. For code review, you might allow access to online documentation while keeping source files read-only. Users configure the Codex sandbox through permission profiles , which define the filesystem and network restrictions for a Codex session. In this article, we’ll start with the tradeoffs behind Codex’s sandbox defaults, then explain the sandbox’s design and how the harness uses it to run commands. We’ll show how end users and enterprises can tailor its permissions to their needs and how developers can reuse the sandbox in their own tools. Finally, we’ll examine how these restrictions are enforced on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Choosing the sandbox boundaries In Codex, our philosophy is to specify conservative defaults for the sandbox that still enable meaningful work. For example, with a Git repository as the workspace root, the built-in :workspace permission profile: Allows writes within the workspace, while keeping directories such as .git and .codex read-only. items.title: 人生不过三万天，Anthropic一万亿
items.desc:
Anthropic上市前夕，达里奥·阿莫代伊与摩根大通CEO杰米·戴蒙做了一次访谈。被问到“为什么现在上市”，达叔表示自己也是第一次去敲钟，因此咨询过很多人的建议：

 其中最常见、也最让我有共鸣的建议——虽然大家表述各异，但意思是一样的： 绝对不要让你的公司比它的真实价值多哪怕一美元。 

 好好好，那么Anthropic的真实价值是多少？

 今年8月，投资机构按2028年1900亿-2000亿美元收入，直接给Anthropic估2万亿美元。生意可以慢慢做，身价先一步计算到位。

 10月14日，Anthropic举办投资者活动，披露公司三季度收入环比增长45%。活动现场，Anthropic还为投资机构定做了一批印有“thinking”字样的帽子。

 按照路透报道，被扣帽子的机构也走了心，经过一轮深度思考，给出了1.5万亿的新估值。

 

 Anthropic发给投资者的thinking小帽

 到了11月10日，Anthropic公布IPO发行价格区间，估值又掉到了1-1.4万亿美元（完全摊薄）。

 但Anthropic同期的业绩非常炸裂。今年前三个季度，公司收入分别为47亿、116亿和170亿美元。到10月底，ARR达到810亿美元，环比增长100亿。

 生意越做越大，身价越谈越低。恒生科技指数和改变人类命运的Frontier lab，居然也能找到共同语言。

 二阶导数 
 大模型公司炒的一直是二阶导数，即增长的加速度。既要看增长，更要看增长的增长；光进步不行，进步速度还要快。

 AI的大规模商业化今年才开始。去年年底，Anthropic的ARR“只有”90亿美元，今年4月超过300亿美元，5月超过470亿美元。

 半年不到规模翻了五倍多，按年观测的指标，开始按月刷新机构的认知。

 ARR常用于SaaS公司，由于SaaS公司的收入要随服务提供逐期确认，新签客户的全年订阅无法体现在当期收入里，ARR可以提前反映公司整体业务规模。

 Anthropic招股书使用的名称是 Run-Rate Revenue ，计算方法是 最近28天的按量收费额×13＋当前月度订阅费×12 （有些鸡贼公司用的一周×52）。

 招股书同时说明，这个指标不能替代会计收入，也不是未来收入预测。

 但资本市场管你这那的。按 官方+媒体披露 和 TickerTrends 两种口径，会发现Anthropic的ARR一直在增长，但增长加速度的峰值，出现在二季度。

 今年7月，Anthropic ARR摸到650亿美元，加速度也非常可观。到了8月，机构给出了2万亿美元的估值。这个估值未必是按7月的加速度外推，但肯定隐含了机构对加速度的预期。

 但到了三季度，Anthropic新增ARR掉头向下，加速度失速。

 

 

 官方和TickerTrends的披露节点间隔天数不同，新增ARR不太可比。用一个区间的新增ARR平均，再换算成30天的ARR增长均值（非实际新增额），也能得出一个类似的结论：

 Anthropic的增长加速度在下滑。 

 

 因此，路透在10月的报道明确提出：机构把估值调到1.5万亿美元，原因是对三季度环比增速放缓感到失望。

 用同样的口径观测OpenAI的增长加速度，会发现OpenAI在三季度也有相对明显的下滑。9月底，OpenAI按1.4万亿美元融资，结果等到11月才按1.25万亿估值拿到了钱，比最初目标低了11%。

 

 

 也就是说，AI商业化今年开始后，增长速度远超预期，急躁资本毫不犹豫给出了很高的估值。一旦增长节奏放缓，机构会重新判断增长曲线能否兑现。

 到了四季度，两家公司纷纷重新提速。

 按照OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar的口径，三季度收入约100亿美元，环比增长50%。季度末年化收入约500亿美元，整个三季度内增长约70%。

 Anthropic的增长更快。10月ARR从9月的710亿美元涨到约810亿美元，一个月增加100亿美元，超过此前两个月的增幅。虽然加速度绝对值不及年初，但增长势头重新增强。

 然而，Anthropic11月公布的发行估值仍然下滑。既然增长已经重新提速，投资机构还在顾虑什么？

 先苦后甜 
 今年10月，Anthropic的ARR重新提速。但招股书里算了另一笔账：

 二季度，Anthropic环比多做了68亿美元收入，购买算力的基础设施费用环比多花了22亿。三季度，收入增加54亿，算力成本增加43亿。

 

 环比增长的收入减少，算力开支倒是快翻倍了。

 今年的三个季度，Anthropic收入环比增速从132%降到47%，算力开支环比增速从15%增长到77%。每100美元收入对应的新增算力开支，从16美元涨到了80美元。

 招股
items.summary: Anthropic IPO 估值从 2 万亿美元降至 1-1.4 万亿，尽管其 ARR 在四季度环比增长 45% 达 810 亿美元。分析指出市场开始关注增长加速度的二阶导数，而非单纯规模。
items.reason: 独特地用“二阶导数”视角解析了顶级 AI 公司估值的波动逻辑，揭示了资本市场对 AI 商业化加速度而非绝对值敏感的投资心理，对理解 AI 融资趋势有深层启示。

items.title: [开源] 给 Sub2API 做了个降智巡检工具，支持自动剔除、冷却复测、通过恢复
items.desc:
最近在折腾 Sub2API 的账号池，做了个模型质量巡检工具，分享给有同样需求的佬友。

 一个分组里挂了好几个上游账号，接口都能正常返回，但有的账号碰到同一道题就是答不好。我想做的是让 Sub2API 自己定时出题、记录结果，发现异常就先把那个账号移出调度，等复测过了再放回来。
可以直接嵌进 Sub2API
巡检服务用 Docker Compose 单独部署，连上已有的 Sub2API，再加一个自定义菜单，就能在原来的面板里打开巡检页面。沿用 Sub2API 登录，无需改网关源码。 管理员可以配置巡检，普通用户也能选自己的 Key 测一轮。
自动剔除后，怎么恢复？
举个例子，给一个分组设成每小时巡检一次，选一道逻辑题和一道 JSON 题。如果某个账号明确答错了标准答案题，开启自动剔除后，巡检就会暂时停用这个账号的调度。

 冷却结束后，系统会单独复测原账号。这时候账号还在暂停调度，全部复测题通过才会恢复接单。 如果没通过，就继续冷却。遇到超时、限额之类的请求问题，巡检可以按优先级换同组账号，结果也会单独记录。

 自动剔除默认关闭，可以先跑几轮看看结果，再决定要不要开。
能测哪些题？
内置了糖果题、逻辑选择题、数值计算、JSON 指令遵循、指纹观察、鹈鹕骑自行车。每个分组可以多选题目，还能改题干、标准答案和每题请求次数。

 有标准答案的题可以自动判。像「鹈鹕骑自行车」这类题，可以直接在结果页看 SVG 作品，也能翻历史，把不同时间的回答放在一起看。单轮答错适合当排查线索，判断模型表现有多稳定，可以多看几轮。

 项目基于 NoonWake.AI 的 AI Drool Router 二次开发。欢迎佬友试用，尤其想听听大家平时都用什么题来测模型，或者希望巡检遇到什么情况时自动暂停账号。项目地址
 https://github.com/daQzi/code1024-drool-router
items.summary: 开源工具基于 Drool Router 二次开发，为 Sub2API 提供模型质量巡检。支持定时出题、自动剔除异常账号、冷却后复测恢复。内置逻辑、JSON 等测试题，支持 Docker Compose 独立部署，无需修改网关源码，可自定义巡检策略。
items.reason: 针对多账号池管理中的质量不稳定问题，提供了自动化检测与动态调度的解决方案，包含具体的冷却复测机制，对需要管理大量 API 账号的运维或开发团队极具实用价值。

items.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
items.desc: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining. To benchmark these capabilities, we introduce HH-Bench, comprising 12 tasks involving teams of 2 to 10 humanoids, including heterogeneous teams. Systematic evaluations show that Heave-Ho consistently outperforms baseline methods, while real-world experiments demonstrate robust decentralized collaboration across challenging tasks.

Streaming MoE experts directly from SSD gets within 6% of Strata on token generation. 

 I've been trying to rely less on online models and run bigger ones locally.
At home I have a PC with two RTX 4090s (let's call it Orthrus - the two-headed hound
of Greek mythology), and for work I have a MacBook M5 with 32G of unified memory.

 Orthrus runs on Windows 11, because my kids play games all the time. I had a
dual boot with Ubuntu, but their games ended up taking most of the two
terabytes of disk.

 I am also a huge fan of RMD (rooms moving development): one hour in the kitchen
sipping my coffee, two hours at my office desk, then the sofa. A fixed desktop
tower is not for me.

 My first experiment was to run Qwen 3.8 27B with llama.app on Orthrus and use
it from my laptop through pi . That model does the coding tasks, an online
model like Opus does the orchestration, and the second RTX runs a FIM model for
auto-completion in Neovim.

 When I talked about this on social networks, I got very strong feedback: use
 Strata with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next .

 
 
 
 
 
What is Strata?
 
 
 Strata is an inference engine for MoE models like Qwen. Only the hot experts
stay in VRAM, the rest goes to RAM, or even to disk. Experts are 90%+ of a MoE
model's weights, so a 180B model like this one can run on a GPU with much less
memory. Like my RTX 4090!

 It works on a laptop too, and I stumbled on

exactly that: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on a 32 GB Mac M4, faster than llama.cpp , at
13.5 tok/s.

could run at a decent speed.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.desc: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learning and constructs from machine learning literature on self-generated curricula. Furthermore, we study the extent to which the learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks, observing improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation.

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.desc:
📄 Paper | 🤗 Data | 💻 Code 

 

 Truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail. We’re releasing XYBench , a benchmark of 8K+ questions that tests how AI assistants respond to requests based on misconceptions, such as asking how to thicken frosting that keeps sliding off cupcakes when the real problem is that the cupcakes are still too warm to frost. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026.

 A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem : a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y. In the cupcake example, the person is so committed to making the frosting stick that they fail to consider the warmth of the cupcake as the true problem to be addressed.

 Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal. Drawing on 8,115 real-world questions spanning programming and everyday activities such as cooking and home repair, we introduce a benchmark that measures whether models identify these misconceptions and are able to prioritize effective solutions in their responses.

 The models we evaluated on XYBench – Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro – often suggested a solution to the user’s problem but kept their answers focused on the original, mistaken approach. Unlike human reference answers, all five models were less likely to steer users away from that approach and toward a solution suited to their goal.

 People use AI systems with different levels of knowledge and may not always know how best to approach a problem. We hope XYBench helps

items.title: 智谱新模型，490 tokens/s！
items.desc:
GLM「速度仙人」来了？

 听雨 发自 凹非寺

量子位 | 公众号QbitAI

 智谱上新了一个 GLM-5.3-Highspeed 模型，就在Zcode里。

 据网友@leo114119爆料，这个新模型目前已经在Zcode 3.15.1里开放体验，订阅用户随机获得。

 
 
 
 
 
 
 他晒出来的速度，甚至达到了 490 tokens/s 。

 
 
 
 我也第一时间去Zcode里试了试，尝试手动添加并切换了这个模型。

 
 
 
 但不知道是因为Lite套餐用户还不具备享受资格，还是因为没灰度到😭。。。

 只能先望洋兴叹了(：з」∠)

 GLM-5.3高速版来了？

 既然是高速模型，那最值得关注的当然是 速度 了。

 490TPS ——这个网友晒出来的速度数字，也是相当恐怖了，接近500TPS。

 TPS指的是每秒生成的token数量。如果持续保持这一速度，输出1万token，单算生成阶段约需20秒。

 要知道，上个月智谱刚发布的GLM-5.3-FlashX，最高速度也才200 tokens/s。

 而按照Artificial Analysis的测速，GLM-5.3-Flash在Z.ai API上的输出速度约为60 tokens/s。

 这新模型是什么速度仙人啊？？？

 而且GLM-5.3-Highspeed这个名字，此前已有迹象。

 Pi的模型目录已经收录了GLM-5.3-Highspeed。

 
 
 
 在这份目录中，GLM-5.3-Highspeed上下文窗口为100万token，最大生成token上限为131,072，约128k；还划分了low、high、max三档思考强度配置。

 不过，这些配置与GLM-5.3普通版也都是一致的。

 此外，也有网友在reddit上讨论过这款新模型，并猜测它是否与OpenCode上的匿名模型 Omen Alpha 有关。

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Omen Alpha在9月份刚刚上新OpenCode，基本已经被网友扒出来与GLM有关。

 
 
 
 还有网友实测了下鹈鹕踩单车的水平。。

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 总结来说就是： 速度快，思考久，效果还蛮好 。

 至于Omen Alpha到底是什么模型，也是众说纷纭。

 有人说它就是GLM-5.3-Highspeed，也有人猜GLM-5.3-Omni、GLM-5.4-Flash。

 此前，智谱也推出过高速版模型。

 今年5月，智谱推出了 GLM-5.1-highspeed ，模型输出速度为400tokens/s，在当时基本也是刷新了全球大模型厂商API的速度上限。

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 这回的GLM-5.3-Highspeed如果真能达到490 TPS的水平，那对于长程任务来说，速度也是相当可观的了。

 
 
 
 目前这款新模型还在Zcode里随机灰度中，如果有灰度到的网友，欢迎分享你的实测体验呀！！
items.summary: 智谱在 Zcode 平台上线 GLM-5.3-Highspeed，网友实测输出速度达 490 tokens/s。该模型拥有 100 万上下文，分三档思考强度，此前被猜测为 OpenCode 上的匿名模型 Omen Alpha。

items.title: 一份看空中际旭创的报告，戳中了AI硬件的最大软肋
items.desc:
一份看空中际旭创的估值测算，几乎把整个AI硬件资产的估值困境摆到了台面上。

 11月17日，一份关于中际旭创的看空测算在投资圈迅速传播。按照这份材料的预测，到2029年，中际旭创的年净利润大约只有300亿元，对应合理市值3000亿至4500亿元。

 考虑到折现因素，即使在最乐观的情况下，公司目前的股价仍然存在约25%的回撤空间。

 这份测算一出，便迅速引发了极大的争议。

 要知道，中际旭创今年的业绩可以说相当惊人。2026年前三季度，公司实现营业收入695.47亿元，同比增长178.13%；归母净利润222.38亿元，同比增长211.81%。按此计算，归母净利率接近32%。

 不仅的经营数据仍然相当强劲，订单、产品价格和毛利率并没有出现明显恶化。

 卖方机构甚至还在不断上调盈利预期。10月底，华泰证券预计中际旭创2026年至2028年的归母净利润分别达到335亿元、807亿元和1132亿元。

 一边是2028年净利润突破千亿元的乐观预期，另一边却是2029年净利润只有300亿元的看空测算。对于中际旭创这样一家备受市场关注的AI硬件龙头，未来盈利预期竟然能相差数倍，实在少见。

 事实上，中际旭创面临的分歧，也是整个AI硬件的缩影。

 就在今天，英伟达公布了最新三季报，营收依然保持着惊人的增长。但另一边，随着股价回落，其预期市盈率已经降至约12倍，创下2012年以来的低位。

 明明业绩还在高速增长，市场却对AI硬件资产产生了巨大的担忧。这也是为什么一份建立在2029年假设之上的测算，会在此时引起如此大的反应。

 300亿元利润，是怎么算出来的？ 
 我们先来说说，这300亿元利润究竟是怎么算出来的。整个计算过程其实很简单，分为四步。

 第一步，假设2029年全球AI资本开支达到8000亿美元 。

 这个数字并非凭空而来。11月13日，半导体研究机构SemiAnalysis更新了AI加速器资本开支预测，将2029年的预测值从1.352万亿美元下调至7960亿美元，降幅高达41%。

 背后主要有三个担忧：AI应用收入不及预期、数据中心融资受阻，以及AI芯片的高溢价难以持续。

 第二步，光互连能分走多少预算？ 

 这份测算假设，到2029年，可插拔光模块和NPO等近封装光互连，合计占AI硬件资本开支的7%。其中，跨服务器、跨机柜的Scale-out互连占5%，机柜内、加速器之间的Scale-up互连贡献另外2%。

 按照8000亿美元计算，对应560亿美元的光互连市场。

 第三步，假设中际旭创拿下50%的市场份额 。

 这个假设其实相当乐观。目前，中际旭创在全球高速数通光互连市场的份额约为28.1%。如果到2029年达到50%，意味着还要提升21.9个百分点。

 当然，这并非完全没有可能。中际旭创在800G市场的份额已经超过40%，而在1.6T等新一代产品上，市场估算其份额甚至达到50%—70%。

 随着AI数据中心网络速率不断升级，高端产品占比提升，中际旭创确实有机会进一步扩大市场份额。

 但问题在于，未来的光互连市场，并不是现有产品的简单延伸。

 Scale-out和Scale-up的技术需求不同，NPO、CPO和可插拔光模块等技术路线之间，也存在竞争和替代关系。一家企业今天在800G、1.6T上占据优势，并不意味着未来一定能在整个光互连市场拿下50%的份额。

 不过，即便按照这个乐观假设，8000亿美元资本开支对应560亿美元光互连市场，中际旭创拿下一半，就意味着280亿美元收入，折合人民币约1890亿元。

 第四步，也是最关键的一步，假设净利率降至15% 。

 这个数字明显低于当下的水平。要知道，今年前三季度，中际旭创的归母净利率约为32%。

 按照15%计算，1890亿元收入最终只能产生约283.5亿元净利润，测算中取整按300亿元计算。

 接下来，再给予10至15倍市盈率，对应2029年3000亿至4500亿元市值。以三年为周期，按照8%至12%的折现率折回当下，估值区间落在2135亿至3572亿元。

 如果以4850亿元的市值作为参考，中性情形对应约44%的下跌空间，即便最乐观的情形，也存在约26%的回撤空间。

 看到这里，大家应该发现了一个很有意思的地方。

 这份看空测算，一边假设中际旭创能够拿下全球一半的光互连市场，一边又认为它的净利率会从32%降至15%，几乎腰斩。

 这看起来有些矛盾。毕竟，按照通常的商业逻辑，市场份额越高，规模效应越明显，企业的盈利能力往往也会更强。

 那么，为什么这份测算在市场份额上如此乐观，却对盈利能力如此悲观？咱们接着往下说。

items.title: 从“能写代码”到“能交付”：腾讯轻量云 LoopForge 云端 Loop实践
items.desc:
采访嘉宾 | 江露
 策划 | 康悦 Rita
 
 
 导语：AI Coding 正在从辅助开发工具走向软件研发流程。代码生成本身已经不再是唯一问题，企业更关心的是：Agent 能否理解完整任务？能否协同完成多个研发环节？能否在长任务中保持上下文和状态一致？最终生成的代码，又能否通过验证并进入稳定交付？围绕这些问题，InfoQ 与腾讯轻量云研发专家江露进行了会前交流。她即将于 AICon 北京站分享《从“能写代码”到“能交付”：腾讯轻量云 LoopForge 云端 Loop实践 》，探讨 AI 如何从“会写代码”进一步走向“能够完成任务”。 
 
 
 一、 面对从“个人提效”到“团队信任”的软件交付难题 
 
 在 AI Coding 应用的早期，团队首先关注的是代码生成的速度和准确性。但当 Agent 开始参与完整的研发流程，评价它的标准也随之变化。
 
 江露说，问题已经从“AI 写代码快不快、准不准”，转向““AI 产出的结果能不能被团队信任、接手和合入”。这份信任，取决于需求和验收标准由谁确认，结果由谁验证，失败后由谁接住，以及同样的做法换一个项目还能否继续使用。
 
 在实际推进中，江露发现，从代码生成到完整交付，有几处容易断开的环节。首先，Agent 获得的信息并不完整。第三方接口约定、业务规则、测试数据和环境配置，大多不在代码仓库里。开发者熟悉的背景知识，对 Agent 而言可能完全不可见。缺少这些信息，它只能依靠推测继续执行。
 
 其次，验证能力未必跟得上代码产出。人工逐行 Review 容易成为瓶颈，而让 Agent 自测自评，又可能出现“自己证明自己是对的”的情况。需求、评审意见和测试结果如果还散落在不同工具与会话中，交接就仍然依靠人来转述。每个角色都在工作，整个任务却需要人不断推动。
 
 更容易造成误判的，是对“完成”的理解不一致。流程跑完、提出合并请求（MR）、代码实际合入、业务验收通过，分别代表不同的进展。混在一起看，就会高估真正完成的交付。
 
 回顾团队的实践，江露说“出问题最多的是两头，中间的编码实现反而相对稳定。”一头是需求理解：需求存在歧义、隐含约束没有写出来、验收标准模糊，Agent 就可能做出一个“看起来合理但不是要的”结果。另一头是验证与合入：测试没有自动化不具备AI修改自动Loop验证(改 → 验证 → 打回 → 再改)的条件，测试环境与实际环境不一致，甚至代码已经修改，使用的仍是旧的检查报告。
 
 在分析原因时，团队也没有把问题全部归结为模型能力。江露认为：“模型能力决定上限，但大多数失败我们最后归因到工程机制上。”
 
 上下文是否真正被读取，验收标准是否可检查，评审与测试是否独立，失败后能否带着原因回到相应环节，都直接影响最终结果。更强的模型并不会自动补齐这些缺口。对于团队而言，下一步需要明确的是将需求确认、产物交接、结果验证和失败处理写入可执行的 SOP，让原本依靠人提醒和补位的环节，有明确的执行规则。
 
 
 二、 不能让 Agent 协作放任自流，把团队共识写成可执行的 SOP 
 
 早期团队也曾期待 Agent 自由编排整个任务。但长任务运行起来后，一些问题逐渐暴露：执行路径不稳定，出错后难以定位原因，团队已经约定好的检查步骤也可能被跳过。多 Agent 协作过程中，每个 Agent 都完成了自己的任务，但整体任务却没有真正完成。
 
 江露由此提出一个很实际的判断：“研发流程本身是团队已有的共识，比如先分析再实现、实现后必须评审和测试，没有必要每次让模型重新‘发明’一遍。”
 
 所以团队开始将共识写成可执行的 SOP：用 DAG（有向无环图）定义节点之间的先后依赖，程序负责状态流转、检查与交接，Agent 在节点内完成分析、设计和实现。返工则沿单独声明的回退路径执行。
 
 这样，流程便有了可追溯的执行依据：每次运行固定流程版本，事后能查清当时按什么规则执行；失败可以定位到具体节点，定向返工，不需要从头重来。检查步骤不会被 Agent 绕过，没有前置依赖的节点则可以并行。
 SOP 规定了执行顺序，也明确了每个节点接收什么、产出什么，以及可以使用哪些工具。方案、代码变更和检查报告会通过文件交接，并保留每次尝试的快照，让下游能够核对所用产物的版本，而不是依赖上一环节的自然语言转述。
 
 写进 SOP 的规则，则主要来三类经验：反复踩过的坑、角色交接处容易遗漏的约定，以及只有老员工知道的事。例如，需求没有说清就开始编码，团队便把需求说明和验收确认前置；测试环境如何搭建、执行前需要做哪些准备，也要写下来，成为 Agent 可以使用的上下文。
 
 至于每一步交给谁，团队的原则是：步骤明确、结果能够通过命令判断的工作，交给脚本；需要理解和判断、输出又能够被检
items.summary: 腾讯专家江露探讨 AI 从代码生成到团队信任交付的断层，指出失败多归因于上下文缺失与验证机制不足，而非模型能力上限。需建立独立验证闭环与清晰的验收标准以实现自动化 Loop。
items.reason: 从工程落地角度剖析了 AI Coding 的“最后 100 米”难题，提出了“信任边界”与“验证独立性”的关键观点，为构建可靠 Agent 工作流提供了具体的工程实践指南。

items.title: 业务本体：面向 AI 与数据分析，统一规范业务概念与指标口径 ｜ 技术趋势
items.desc:
2026 年，智能体将在企业级应用中取得哪些实质性突破？ 点击下载 《2026 年 AI 与数据发展预测》白皮书，获悉专家一手前瞻，抢先拥抱新的工作方式！
 
 11 月 3 日，我们宣布推出 Business Ontology ，即将开启公开预览。它提供了一种受治理的方式，支持团队定义、归属、审批共用业务术语、实体、关联关系与指标，并将其映射至承载这些定义的数据和模型。Business Ontology 隶属于 Snowflake Horizon Context ，也就是 Horizon Catalog 内的受治理上下文层。它让人员与 AI 智能体共用同一套经过审批的标准定义，使智能体能够按照业务口径解读企业数据。团队可在各类智能体和应用中复用这套业务知识，无需为每个工具重复定义，同时保留销售、财务、营销等不同业务域的差异。
 
 举例来说，当智能体处理收入相关查询时，它需要清楚财务口径下收入如何定义，以及收入和订单、客户之间的关联关系。这类业务知识通常分散在 BI 模型、dbt 项目以及资深员工的经验里。每当新增一个智能体，团队往往都要重新搭建一遍相关逻辑。一旦智能体理解出现偏差，大家就会依据错误的数据做出决策，进而丧失对 AI 输出结果的信任。而 Business Ontology，就是供团队统一存放官方业务知识的唯一底座。
 
 
 
 整合全域数据资产知识，构建权威业务上下文 
 
 Horizon Context 汇聚团队现有各类工具中的业务知识。其开箱即用的元数据连接器，可从Tableau、Power BI、dbt、SQL Server、Sigma、Omni、 PostgreSQL 等数据源采集 schema、查询日志、看板定义以及使用行为信号。依托跨平台数据血缘，系统可追踪数据从源数据库到看板、历经多层转换的完整链路，形成连通的数据资产全景视图，让团队掌握 Snowflake 内外数据的来源与使用情况。
 
 为使智能体可信调用上下文，Snowflake 提供了三层上下文，各司其职： Snowflake Cortex Sense（即将开启公开预览）自动推断上下文，Business Ontology 治理业务含义，Snowflake Semantic Views 执行指标计算。
 
 为何拆分为三层而非一层？因为每一层解决的问题各不相同，没有任何单一能力可以同时兼顾这三件事。Cortex Sense 帮助智能体快速广泛覆盖数据资产，无需团队提前手动定义每张数据表和每一项指标。Business Ontology 在核心环节注入权威口径，确保人员与智能体统一遵循经过审批的业务定义。Semantic Views 保障计算精准度，保证各项指标每次都以一致规则运算。
 
 这三层不存在固定先后顺序。客户可以优先选用最贴合自身迫切需求的一层，再随着业务发展叠加其余能力。有的团队从术语表切入，有的团队会优先落地可执行指标。无论从哪一层切入，这三层能力都可为所有智能体、应用及人员提供统一、权威的业务上下文。
 
 下面我们逐层展开。
 
 借助 Cortex Sense 实现上下文自动化 
 
 对不少团队来说，Cortex Sense 是很自然的切入点，大量底层工作都由它自动完成。它会持续观测用户查询数据、搭建看板、运行数据管道的行为并采集上下文，再把这些日常操作沉淀为业务认知，以此降低团队手动定义每张数据表、各项指标含义及关联关系的成本。
 
 Cortex Sense 依托团队已有的元数据和使用行为模式构建上下文，涵盖查询历史、看板、dbt 模型等资产。它会跟随业务变化同步迭代自身认知，并按照预设周期自动更新知识库。团队只需锁定业务应用场景、接入现有相关上下文，再借助反馈和评估持续调优，无需为每张数据表手动建模。除此之外，Cortex Sense 还可自动识别相互矛盾的业务信息，并提请团队确认可信来源。
 
 当团队准备对核心业务术语开展治理时，Cortex Sense 可在 Business Ontology 中生成初始草稿，自动给出推荐定义、关联关系以及数据链路，团队无需从零搭建。大家只需锁定业务应用场景、接入已有相关上下文，再通过反馈与评估加以打磨，从而免去了手动为每张表建模的负担。与此同时，Cortex Sense 能够智能识别存在冲突的业务信息，提请团队确认可信来源。
 
 借助 Business Ontology 定义业务上下文 
 
 Business Ontology 是团队统一登记核心业务术语的定义、责任人以及相互关联关系的载体。以 “净收入” 为例，不必再让每个语义视图、看板和智能体各持一个版本，分析师只需定义一次（或从现有术语表导入），把作用域设为“财务”，指定责任人，完成审批，再把它关联到语义视图里
items.summary: Snowflake 推出 Business Ontology，通过治理层统一业务术语与指标定义，映射至数据模型。支持 Tableau、dbt 等工具接入，使人与 AI 共用同一套业务口径，避免决策偏差。
items.reason: 指出了 AI 数据分析中“语义对齐”的关键缺失环节，提供了具体的产品化解决方案（三层上下文架构），对于希望让 AI 准确理解企业内部数据的分析师极具实用价值。

items.title: RAW: Refusal Aversion in the Wild, A Causal Measurement Method for Deployed LLMs
items.desc:
arXiv:2611.21641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deployed LLMs field hundreds of millions of conversations a day and refuse a non-trivial fraction of user requests, yet the user-side cost of refusal, whether users disengage and by how much, is unmeasured on any production model: a blind spot for the consumer-facing platforms built on them. A/B-testing refusal is ethically and operationally constrained on frontier-lab products and unavailable to third-party platforms deploying these models through a fixed API. We introduce RAW, a method that uses LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment: at near-identical prompts in any existing log, the same model sometimes refuses and sometimes does not, and that variation identifies the causal user-side effect of refusal. Applying the method to 15 deployed LLMs in LMSYS-Chat-1M and WildChat, with user-clustered inference, we find that for about half of the models we can measure precisely, a refusal costs 3 to 17 pp of subsequent re-engagement; the rest show no distinguishable effect, among them one deployment whose positive point estimate we trace to persistent users retrying the refused request. Our contribution is the measurement method, which runs on any deployed model from logs alone for about \$0.30 per 1,000 conversations. We release labels, moderation scores, prompt embeddings, and pipeline code.
items.titleCn: RAW：LLM 拒绝行为的因果测量方法
items.summary: 提出 RAW 方法，利用 LLM 随机性作为自然实验，测量生产环境中拒绝请求的因果影响。在 15 个部署模型上发现，约半数模型的拒绝导致后续再参与度下降 3-17 个百分点，其余无显著差异。
items.reason: 提供了首个可复现的因果推断框架，量化“拒绝”对用户体验的实际成本，帮助平台方优化安全策略与留存率的平衡。

items.title: FieldGuide: A Corpus Map for Token-Efficient Agentic Document Exploration
items.desc:
arXiv:2611.21647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI agents can help journalists explore large document collections. But exploratory workflows can require substantial token use and time, especially when the task is broad and the relevant subquestions are not yet known. This paper introduces FieldGuide, an agent-facing corpus map that organizes a document collection into a topic hierarchy and exposes tools for corpus orientation, scoped search, and bounded reading. I evaluate FieldGuide on five journalistic document-exploration tasks using 38 Chicago Police Department public-records documents, comparing it with raw-file access and retrieval-augmented generation. Across the five tasks, FieldGuide used 27% fewer tokens and 41% less elapsed time than raw-file access; relative to RAG, it used 38% fewer tokens and 21% less elapsed time. An accuracy audit identified four minor issues in FieldGuide's responses, comparable to the other conditions. In blind ratings of generated reporting leads, FieldGuide's mean ratings were higher than RAG's and lower than the raw-file condition's. These descriptive results suggest that corpus orientation may reduce runtime token use and elapsed time without severe accuracy failures. They also motivate further study of whether selective access limits broad, cross-document discovery.
items.titleCn: FieldGuide：面向 Agent 的语料库地图
items.summary: 提出 FieldGuide 框架，将文档集组织为层级主题地图，供 Agent 进行范围搜索和有限阅读。在新闻探索任务中，相比原始文件访问减少 27% token 消耗和 41% 时间，相比 RAG 减少 38% token。
items.reason: 解决 Agent 在大规模文档探索中的 token 效率痛点，提供具体的性能提升数据，为构建低成本文档分析 Agent 提供工程实践参考。

items.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
items.desc: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. Our new cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline converts existing RGB videos into demonstrations for alternative embodiments by retargeting the recovered motion and synthesizing the corresponding observations, without recorded source-robot states. Experiments show that the tracker achieves absolute trajectory errors of 7.60 and 16.07 mm on DROID and RoboLab and adapts to a new embodiment with only ten demonstrations. The generator achieves 69.19% mean success on RoboTwin and outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks, while joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.
items.titleCn: TCP4D：机器人操控统一跟踪与生成模型
items.summary: 提出 TCP4D 模型，基于 4D 场景表示统一跟踪机器人工具中心点并生成未来轨迹。新增强数据管道可将 RGB 视频转换为不同具身环境的演示，跟踪误差在 DROID 上为 7.60mm，仅需 10 个演示适应新环境。
items.reason: 解决跨具身机器人演示数据稀缺问题，提供具体的跟踪精度和适应效率数据，对提升机器人泛化能力的研究具有参考价值。

items.title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
items.desc: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops. The method decomposes this complex task into a chain of simple visual decisions about what to construct and what to correct. Geometric tools support precise construction, allowing the agent to focus on visual reasoning. Using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model, CADMAGEDDON outperforms prior approaches, including systems based on frontier models, in reconstruction quality on all the main benchmarks. CADMAGEDDON integrates with FreeCAD, bringing its reconstructions into practitioners' existing CAD workflows. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/cadmageddon
items.titleCn: CADMAGEDDON：本地推断的高保真 CAD 重建
items.summary: 开源 Agent CADMAGEDDON，可在单 GPU 或笔记本电脑上运行，将网格重建为可编辑 CAD。使用 Qwen3.8-27B 模型，在主要基准上优于基于前沿模型的系统，并集成 FreeCAD。
items.reason: 降低 CAD 自动化门槛，强调本地化部署的隐私与成本优势，提供具体的模型选型（27B）和工作流集成方案，适合中小企业应用。

items.title: google-research/paper-orchestra
items.desc:
PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.
 https://yiwen-song.github.io/paper_orchestra/ 
 
 
 🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing
 
 
 Yiwen Song
 1 , Yale Song
 1 , Tomas Pfister
 1 , and Jinsung Yoon
 1 
 
 
 1 Google Cloud AI Research
 

 
 PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams.
 
 Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
 
 
 
 
 Key Features 
 
 Multi-Agent Pipeline : Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation. 
 Comprehensive Literature Synthesis : Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript. 
 Visuals Generation : Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams. 
 LaTeX Automation : Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates.

items.title: Managing frontier AI risk: From training to deployment
items.desc:
Defense in depth across the model lifecycle Defense in depth across the model lifecycle During research: contain models in sandboxed environments Internal deployment: test alignment, closely monitor behavior External deployment: protect against misuse and misalignment at scale Incident Response and Disclosure Related research and resources Defense in depth across the model lifecycle During research: contain models in sandboxed environments Internal deployment: test alignment, closely monitor behavior External deployment: protect against misuse and misalignment at scale Incident Response and Disclosure Related research and resources The capabilities of frontier models are rapidly accelerating, and our ability to understand, align, and secure them must stay ahead. We are pacing the development and release of our models, including pausing internal training or holding back models like GPT‑6.1 Astra when we need more time to meet our safety standards. We’ve introduced new processes such as safety cases and require stronger evidence of aligned behavior throughout training. These requirements slow the pace of model releases, but they give us greater confidence to safely move forward. 
 Since the Hugging Face incident  in July, we've strengthened safeguards and alignment requirements for how we train, test, and deploy models. This post explains how we evaluate and manage risk at each stage , from highly sandboxed training environments to the Codex deployment you use on your computer. We evaluate both models and safeguards at each stage, requiring a safety review to advance to the next stage.

items.title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
items.desc:
Predicting end-to-end fine-tuning time on shared GPU clusters, from 272 production runs. 

 A preview of our upcoming paper, Predicting End-to-End Fine-Tuning Time for Generative Language Models . The full version will be on arXiv soon. 

 GPUs are among the most expensive and scarcest resources in AI today. Anyone running a shared cluster has to decide, every day, which jobs go on which GPUs and in what order. That plan is only as good as the estimate of how long each job will take. When a job finishes hours early, GPUs sit idle until the next one is dispatched. When it runs hours late, everything queued behind it slips, experiments wait and delivery dates move.

 Better duration estimates turn this into planning instead of guesswork: what runs, when, and on how many GPUs, with less idle capacity in between. Yet the estimate most teams use is a back-of-the-envelope FLOP calculation. It says nine hours, and the job finishes the next afternoon.

 We wanted to know how far off that math really is, and whether we could do better before a job is even dispatched. So we took 272 real supervised fine-tuning (SFT) jobs from our production pool of NVIDIA H200 GPUs, about 7,382 GPU-hours in total, and compared analytical estimates against learned predictors.

 The short version: the usual FLOP-based estimate explains little of what we observed (R² = 0.31, MAE 12.41 h). A CatBoost regressor that only sees information available before dispatch reaches R² = 0.98, with a mean absolute error of 1.71 h and a median error of 0.51 h in 5-fold cross-validation. The gap comes from two things a closed-form estimate cannot do. The regressor sees more training-specific signals, such as evaluation cadence, checkpoint policy, per-GPU load and fine-tuning regime, and it learns the nonlinear interactions between them from past runs.

items.title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
items.desc:
This walkthrough showcases a beverage can pick-and-place task that uses the UR17G arm , Robotiq 2F-140 gripper , and beverage can to compose a scene in Isaac Sim, check their behavior, and run a pick-and-place example with agent-generated controls.

 For robotics workflows, SimReady means an OpenUSD asset has been prepared with the properties needed for a defined simulation use case, such as collisions, mass, joints, and joint drives. SimReady Central , an open asset library on Hugging Face, lets you reuse robot and object assets with authored simulation properties and profile-validation evidence. For more about the library and its launch, read the announcement blog .

 
 
 
 
 
What makes a robot asset SimReady?
 
 
 SimReady Foundation defines what features the OpenUSD asset needs for a simulation use case. Its specifications connect three levels:

 
 Profile: a group of features for a use case, such as a robot body. 
 Features: capabilities needed for the use case, such as joints that can be controlled. 
 Requirements: checks on the settings needed for each feature, such as a joint’s drive settings. 
 
 For this task, those properties include the arm and gripper’s joints and a beverage can asset collisions and mass. Validation checks these settings against the profile’s requirements. The simulation then tests whether the assembled robot can use them to pick up and move the can.

 
 
 
 
 
What comes with the asset, and what do you add?
 
 
 The UR17G , Robotiq 2F-140 , and beverage can packages include the models and their simulation settings. You assemble the scene and add task code to define the arm–gripper assembly, work surface, starting positions, and controls for moving the arm and opening and closing the gripper.

items.title: CrisisBench: an evaluation suite for crisis counseling AI
items.desc:
arXiv:2611.21622v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Background: Crisis helplines are essential to mental health systems but are often understaffed and underfunded. LLMs could support counselors, but existing benchmarks do not capture the escalation, risk assessment, and de-escalation central to crisis conversations, while privacy restrictions limit use of real transcripts.
Methods: We present CrisisBench, a privacy-preserving suite for single- and multi-turn crisis counseling evaluation. It includes 1,085 single-turn tasks from 200 de-identified conversations and 1,185 patient LLMs derived from hotline metadata. Patient models and a 23-item LLM judge were calibrated against expert counselors.
Results: We evaluated five GPT models plus draft-then-edit and retrieval-augmented generation. All systems underperformed human counselors on excessive empathy and questioning in single-turn evaluation. The rubric achieved human-human Krippendorff's $\alpha$ = 0.51 and LLM-human $\alpha$ = 0.54 (Pearson r = 0.80). In multi-turn evaluation, retrieval-augmented generation scored highest overall (0.961), with all systems within 0.058. Microskills and style/tone were near ceiling, while productivity and safety/risk accounted for most between-system variation. Counselors rated patient LLMs realistic (86%) and useful (92%).
Conclusion: CrisisBench enables scalable, privacy-preserving evaluation of crisis counseling. Current systems perform strongly on core structural competencies but still diverge from experts on important response-level failure modes. We release the rubrics, judge prompts, and evaluation tasks.

items.title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps
items.desc: Learned lossless codecs make smaller files than common classical codecs, yet the images we archive and train on still use classical codecs. A main reason is time: a learned codec takes seconds to decode a photo that a classical codec opens in milliseconds, and their faster variants give up most of their gain in size. We argue that much of this time is spent waiting, not computing: the network waits for the values it conditions on, and the arithmetic decoder reads them one at a time. We introduce FMT (Fixed-step Multiscale Tree), a lossless image format whose decoding order and entropy coder are designed together so that neither wait grows with the image. FMT stores an image as a coarse-to-fine tree whose steps hold independent values: a GPU predicts each step at once and decodes it in parallel rANS lanes that carry their states from step to step, so an image of any size decodes in a fixed number of sequential steps. On this tree we build a family of bit-exact codecs, from a rule with no network to large networks, and no codec we ran on the same GPU beats any of them on both size and speed. Without a network, FMT beats NVIDIA's HTJ2K on size and speed; with a large one, it decodes Kodak photos 9 to 61X faster than learned codecs we ran on the same A100, at the same size or smaller.

items.title: Time-Series Models in the Streamhouse: A New Frontier and Use Cases
items.desc:
Real-time forecasting, anomaly detection, and optimization, powered by IBM time-series models with more than 50 million downloads. Now available natively on Confluent, in the cloud and on premises, running on CPUs. 

 Every business generates a continuous record of change: a machine reading, a payment, a sale, an order, or a change in inventory. These observations form time series, and they carry signals that can help teams anticipate what happens next.

 The challenge is turning those signals into decisions while they still matter. A forecast delivered after a production run, a stockout, or a payment authorization may be accurate, but too late to influence the outcome.

 IBM and Confluent are bringing time-series foundation models closer to the data as it flows. With Apache Flink, teams can apply forecasting , anomaly detection and semantic intelligence to streaming data using SQL, making model outputs available to the applications and people responsible for the next action. 

 Foundation models have changed how organizations work with text, images, and documents. Time-series foundation models extend a similar idea to numerical data by learning general patterns from diverse historical data and then applying that knowledge to new series and tasks. The models can provide a starting point without requiring teams to train a separate model for every series. Depending on the task and deployment, teams can also fine-tune a model or combine its outputs with other data and business logic. 

 

 Figure 1. More than 50 million downloads, and the family of four models behind them 

 Now the time series foundation models run natively inside Confluent as built-in functions in the cloud and on premises. In Confluent Cloud they are fully managed, with nothing to deploy ( documentation ). On premises, the models can run within your own infrastructure using Confluent Platform for Apache Flink.( documentation ). The models run on CPUs, without requiring GPUs.

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.desc:
External sandboxes for coding agents 

I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine.

 I worked on this project with Prime Radiant , the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects .

 My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox.

 To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations:

 
 external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly. 
 external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance. 
 external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package! 
 
 Each of these implementations offers the same localhost API. You can then configure Pi, Claude Code, or Codex to send API calls to that sandbox any time they want to execute code.

 The sandboxes also include an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code is allowed to communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent. Here's the UI you can use to reconfigure that proxy while the sandbox is still running:

 

 I continue to be fascinated by the challenge of safely running untrusted code. This external sandbox pattern provides a neat way to experiment with different approaches.

items.title: jingyaogong/minimind
items.desc:
🧠 Train a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in just 2h!
 https://jingyaogong.github.io/minimind 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 "大道至简" 
 
 
 中文 | English 
 
 
 
 此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。 
 MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。 
 项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。 
 MiniMind 同时拓展了视觉模态模型 MiniMind-V 、多模态 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O 、扩散语言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、线性模型（MiniMind-Linear），详见 Discussion 。 
 项目所有核心算法代码均从 0 使用 PyTorch 原生实现，不依赖第三方库提供的高层抽象接口。 
 这不仅是一个大语言模型全阶段开源复现项目，也是一套面向 LLM 入门与实践的教程。 
 希望此项目能为更多人提供一个可复现、可理解、可扩展的起点，一起感受创造的乐趣，并推动更广泛 AI 社区的进步。 
 
 
 注：本项目基于 Apache 2.0 协议开源，完全免费。“2 小时” 指 SFT 阶段在单张 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 1 epoch 的实测耗时，“3 块钱” 指对应时段的 GPU 租用成本。
 
 
 
 
 
 
 🔗 在线体验 | 🔗 视频介绍 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 📌 项目介绍 
 大语言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出现，引发了全球范围内对 AI 的空前关注。无论是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 还是 Qwen，都以惊艳的效果让人真切感受到这场技术浪潮的冲击力。然而，动辄数百亿参数的模型规模，使得它们对个人设备而言不仅难以训练，甚至连部署都显得遥不可及。打开大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其内部运作机制，本应是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遗憾的是，绝大多数探索最终都止步于使用 LoRA 等技术对现有大模型做少量微调，学习一些新指令或特定任务。这更像是在教牛顿如何使用 21 世纪的智能手机——虽然有趣，却偏离了理解物理本质的初衷。
 
 与此同时，第三方的大模型框架与工具库，如 transformers / trl / peft 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的接口。只需短短十几行代码，就可以完成“加载模型 + 加载数据集 + 推理 + 强化学习”的全流程训练。这种高效封装固然便利，却也在一定程度上把开发者与底层实现隔离开来，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心代码的机会。我认为 “用乐高自己拼出一架飞机，远比坐在头等舱里飞行更让人兴奋”，然而更现实的问题是，互联网上充斥着大量付费课程和营销内容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的讲解包装所谓的 AI 教程。正因如此，本项目的初衷就是尽可能降低 LLM 的学习门槛，让每个人都能从理解每一行代码开始，从 0 开始亲手训练一个极小的语言模型。是的，从 零开始训练 ，而不是仅仅停留在 推理 层面。最低只需不到 3 块钱的服务器成本，就能亲身体验从 0 到 1 构建一个语言模型的全过程。
 
 😊 一起感受创造的乐趣吧！
 
 
 🎉 本项目包含以下内容 
 
 提供完整的 MiniMind-LLM 结构代码（Dense + MoE），当前主线结构对齐 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生态。 
 提供 Tokenizer 与分词器训练代码，支持 <tool_call> 、 <tool_response> 、 <think> 等模板标记。 
 覆盖 Pretrain、SFT、LoRA、RLHF-DPO、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等完整训练流程。 
 提供全阶段开源数据，覆盖收集、蒸馏、清洗与去重后的高质量数据集。 
 关键训练算法与核心模块均从 0 实现，不依赖第三方框架封装。 
 兼容 transformers 、 trl 、 peft 等主流框架，以及 llama.cpp 、 vllm 、 ollama 等常用推理引擎与 Llama-

items.title: Can an LLM dream? Testing the overfitted brain hypothesis on an agent with text memory
items.desc:
arXiv:2611.21648v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hoel (2021) proposed that dreams distort replayed experience so that the brain does not overfit to recent events. We test this hypothesis on an LLM agent (Claude Opus 5.5) that stores what it learns in a text memory and rewrites that memory each night from the day's conversation transcript. The agent goes through ten simulated days of conversation built from LongMemEval. We corrupt 5, 10, 20 or 40 percent of the transcript's turns before each nightly rewrite in one of two ways. Detail corruption changes one or two details in a turn to plausible wrong ones, or replaces the turn with one by the same speaker from an earlier day. Random-text corruption replaces half of the selected turns with a passage of Moby-Dick and inserts Moby-Dick words into the other half. A size limit on the memory, rising from 19,500 to 117,000 tokens over ten nights, set from human free-recall data, forces it to forget. We learned that corruption did not help the agent apply what it learned in earlier conversations to new tasks in any of 30 runs (ten conditions, three different conversation histories). Replacing details in 40 percent of turns lowered recall from 76 to 60 percent. Random text had no consistent effect on recall, with a paired difference of 0 $\pm$ 2 points at 40 percent, because the model recognized it as corrupted and left it out of memory. Replaced details were stored as fact even when another turn held the correct value, and the agent answered 40 percent of those questions correctly, compared with 75 percent without corruption. These results suggest that a pretrained model can separate corrupted text from real events, so a fair test needs a learner that cannot make this separation as easily, such as a model fine-tuned on the corrupted days or an agent whose days take place in an invented world.
